Qué muestran los datos: Entre 2023 y 2025, este organismo adjudicó 24 contratos menores de servicios y suministros de más de 14.000 y hasta 15.000 euros, justo por debajo del límite legal. Si esos importes se repartieran como en la franja inmediatamente inferior, lo esperable serían 3,8 contratos. La razón entre observados y esperados es 6,3, con un intervalo de confianza del 95 % de 3,3 a 12,2. En diciembre se adjudicó el 0 % de los contratos junto al límite, mientras que diciembre supone el 0 % de todos sus contratos de servicios y suministros. Los contratos junto al límite se reparten entre 22 adjudicatarios distintos. El contrato [1], de 14.536 euros, se adjudicó en julio de 2023.
Qué no pueden demostrar: La concentración de contratos al límite no indica malas prácticas. Puede deberse a presupuestos cerrados o necesidades específicas. No hay datos que confirman abusos o errores.
Qué se puede revisar: Comprobar si los contratos al límite abarcan necesidades similares. Verificar si el mismo adjudicatario repite contratos. Analizar si los contratos se distribuyeron uniformemente entre los adjudicatarios.

What the data shows: Between 2023 and 2025, this body awarded 24 minor contracts for services and supplies above 14,000 and up to 15,000 euros, just under the legal limit. If those amounts were spread as in the band immediately below, 3.8 contracts would be expected. The observed-to-expected ratio is 6.3, with a 95% confidence interval of 3.3 to 12.2. December accounts for 0% of the contracts just under the limit, compared with 0% of all its services and supplies contracts. The contracts just under the limit are spread across 22 different awardees. Contract [1], for 14,536 euros, was awarded in July 2023.
What it cannot show: The data shows that some contracts are just under the legal limit, but it doesn't prove any wrongdoing. This could be due to market prices or budget constraints, not necessarily improper actions. The statistical pattern alone doesn't indicate a breach of rules.
What can be checked: Check the details of contract [1] to see what was purchased and the reason for the amount. Verify if multiple contracts were awarded for the same service or need. Look at the distribution of contracts across different awardees to ensure no single provider was favored.
